description: Plan step R1 (graph node rules). The rules board's pure core: the four events, the full rule model with validation, the judge, signals, the built-in default rule with its four peak-level sub-entries, and the code-rule catalog. Depends on FEAT-001. Row wiring comes in FEAT-006; until then the callers are tests and FEAT-005 (checkCall).
steps: Read rules design 0.10 sec 2.2 (field table and the 0.8->0.9 mapping), sec 2.3 (condition vocabulary, event table, filter fields, action table, strength order), sec 2.4, sec 3.1-3.6 (default rule, builtinRulesFor, the three stop sub-entries, reduce sub-entry), sec 10.1 (CatalogEntry), sec 12 (validation limits, at most 50 active rules and 10 with scripts) and sec 15 R1 (the test list and the 'fails today' column). Read impl-plan.md Interpretations 2, 3, 12.

Write the specs first and see them fail (imports of src/rules/judge.ts, builtin.ts, events.ts fail today): extend tests/rules-model.spec.ts; new tests/rules-judge.spec.ts and tests/rules-builtin.spec.ts. Cases: three-valued all/any/not and onUnknown; each condition kind (signal is/in/above/below/known, clock with days/from/to/tz incl. across midnight, stage); field-unreadable means the rule does not match (role, model, session, targetModel); model pattern ^[^/]*/glm equals isGlmModel on a list of ids including openrouter/z-ai/glm-4.6 (no match) and zai/glm-4.6 (match); strongest-wins combine (block > queue > record > inform, ties listed sorted by id); pairing rules (writes filter never with queue; no action never with block; inform only on rules.step; any-tool and glmSpend filters only on builtin entries); builtinRulesFor('inform') = [glm-peak-pricing], ('reduce') adds glm-peak-reduce, ('stop') adds glm-peak-stop, glm-peak-stop-dispatch, glm-peak-stop-scripts; stop level in a peak queues every call of a GLM subagent (role subagent, model GLM) except rules_show, and lets the main agent (GLM and non-GLM) and non-GLM subagents through; reduce queues only glmSpend optional; glm-peak unreadable -> everything passes; inform level and no human rules -> same call gives the same verdict in peak and off-peak; a rule whose action is a script and has no approval is not run and is judged by its onError (allow by default, block on gate.trunk-advance), with the reason text saying the script is not approved on this machine.

Implement: src/rules/events.ts (declarations of gate.tool-call, gate.dispatch, gate.trunk-advance, rules.step using LoopEventDeclaration from src/loops/trigger.ts; gateEvents(...) builds payload+envelope in one place; gate.trunk-advance declared with gateOnErrorDefault 'block' but nothing emits it yet); src/rules/model.ts additions (Effect, RuleTrigger, RuleAction union with ScriptAction, Condition, Rule, BuiltinRule, CatalogEntry, RowState, rule/condition validation per sec 12 using validateWhen with allowGate true); src/rules/judge.ts (judgeInput builds the input for the gate and checkCall from one function, judge, combine); src/rules/signals.ts (effective values: manual over detected, expiry, source, unreadable reason); src/rules/builtin.ts (GLM_PEAK_PRICING, GLM_PEAK_REDUCE, GLM_PEAK_STOP, GLM_PEAK_STOP_DISPATCH, GLM_PEAK_STOP_SCRIPTS, builtinRulesFor, the code-rule CATALOG mapping).

src/guard/catalog.ts: create it (impl-plan Interpretations 3) exporting GUARD_RULES: readonly {id, row, mode, title}[] with the three rules that exist on main (workspace-containment and file-tools-only on row guard, graph-files-only on row graph); mode is the literal 'enforce' for every entry because d-code-rules-enforce removed the shadow mode. builtin.ts maps it to CatalogEntry ids '<row>:<rule id>' and adds rules:files-only (entry only; the gate arrives in FEAT-006). Add a contract test to tests/contracts.spec.ts: every id in the catalog equals the id of a rule object actually installed by that row (import the rule objects from src/guard/rules.ts and src/guard/graph-files.ts; do not keep a second list of ids).
Do not add a row, tool or command in this step. No Node built-in in model.ts (client-importable); judge.ts, signals.ts, builtin.ts may use only the shared library and src/loops/trigger.ts.
Docs in the same commit: docs/ORCHESTRATION.md section 16 gets the model/judge/builtin description (rules events, strength order, built-in entries), docs/DESIGN.md gets the catalog line.
Commit once: 'feat(rules): the rule model, judge and built-in entries (rules)' with gate results.
acceptance_criteria: All R1 cases of design sec 15 that do not need scripts to run, a store or a row pass; the script-without-approval case passes.
src/guard/catalog.ts exists with only rules that exist on main and mode 'enforce'; the contract test ties it to the real rule objects.
The default rule never changes any call's verdict (inform effect only); the three stop sub-entries never touch the main agent.
build, preflight and npm test exit 0 with no new lint/knip/jscpd findings; new specs are listed in package.json.
verification: npm test (TEMP = system temp directory) exits 0

Failing first: all four specs failed with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND on the new src modules before any implementation. npm run probe not run: no host row, patch entry or locale was touched.
baseline failures: none in the gates. Not a gate and not mine: tsc -p tests/tsconfig.json still reports the older-spec errors FEAT-001 listed (for example tests/contracts.spec.ts lines 141 and 149); none in tests/rules-*.spec.ts, tests/rules-fixtures.ts or the lines I added to contracts.spec.ts. package-lock.json stays untracked, never committed.

What exists (all pure, no Node built-in, no clock/file read; callers today are the specs):
- src/rules/events.ts: GATE_EVENTS, GateEvent, RulesEvent, RULES_EVENT_TABLE (the four declarations; only gate.trunk-advance has gateOnErrorDefault 'block'; all personSelectable), RulesEventRecord {event, at, project, session?, payload}, GateCall, gateEvents(call) (gate.tool-call always; gate.dispatch when call.dispatch is given; gate.trunk-advance when call.trunkAdvance is given; the CALLER decides which tool names mean dispatch, nothing in this file knows DISPATCH_TOOL_NAMES), stepEvent(step), modelId({provider?, model?}) -> 'provider/model' or '/model' when the header has no provider.
- src/rules/model.ts (additions): Effect, RuleAction, SignalValue/SignalType/SignalState, Condition, Rule, BuiltinRule, CatalogEntry, RowState (= HealthState | 'absent'), effectOf, RuleContext {now, signals: Map<name, SignalType>, existing: [{id, action}], code?}, validateRule(input, context) -> TriggerIssue[] (paths like id, title, when.events, filter.<key>, action, action.script.file, condition.all[1].signal, lifetime.expiresAt).
- src/rules/judge.ts: judgeInput(parts), evaluateCondition (three-valued), judge(input, rules, {approved?}) -> JudgeResult {effect, hits, strongest, pending, refused, evaluated, subjects}, combine(hits) -> {effect, hits, strongest}, RuleHit {rule, title, effect, ticketPerSession?, reason?}.
- src/rules/signals.ts: GLM_PEAK, SignalReading {name, source, value | unknown}, DetectorStatus, effectiveSignal(name, state, now, detector?).
- src/rules/builtin.ts: GLM_PEAK_PRICING, GLM_PEAK_REDUCE, GLM_PEAK_STOP, GLM_PEAK_STOP_DISPATCH, GLM_PEAK_STOP_SCRIPTS, builtinRulesFor(level), CATALOG (9 entries: guard:workspace-containment, guard:file-tools-only, graph:graph-files-only, rules:files-only, the five builtin:* ids).
- src/guard/catalog.ts: GUARD_RULES (3 entries, mode 'enforce'); tests/contracts.spec.ts ties each id to activeRules(...) of the guard row and graphFilesOnly(...).id of the graph row.
- src/shared/tool-names.ts: RULES_TOOL_NAMES = ['rules_show'].
- tests/rules-fixtures.ts: shared fixtures (NOW is Wednesday 15:00 UTC+8, callOf, inputOf, ruleOf, draftOf, contextOf, peak). Specs listed in package.json test script (rules-judge, rules-builtin after rules-model). Docs: ORCHESTRATION.md sec 16.8 (new) and the 16.6/16.7 edits, DESIGN.md rules row.

What later steps need:
- FEAT-003 (stored rules): validateRule checks the request-shaped rule (origin and status are refused as engine-written). rules.json parsing needs the stored variant (origin/status required and checked); add it next to validateRule. ProjectState has no rules/signals/scripts fields yet; Rule, SignalState exist as types only.
- FEAT-004: SignalState/effectiveSignal take the project state's values; the approved set for judge() is the ids of rules whose scripts[id] entry has approvedAt and a matching hash (FEAT-003 stores it).
- FEAT-005 (checkCall): build events with gateEvents (set caller 'cli'/'library'; set dispatch/trunkAdvance only when known), signals as SignalReading[] (glm-peak source 'caller' | 'heartbeat' | 'clock' | 'none'), pass reasons for unreadable role/model/session through judgeInput({unreadable}). SignalReading has no host (pid) field yet; add it with the heartbeat step.
- FEAT-006 (gate): RULES_TOOL_NAMES already exists with the one name; register rules_show against it and add the contract test there. DISPATCH_TOOL_NAMES does not exist; the gate sets call.dispatch itself. hit.ticketPerSession tells the ticket code to use signature any:<rule>. judge() returns hits sorted strongest-first then by id; hits[].reason is only set for an unapproved script that blocks. JudgeResult.subjects is the 'subjects' column of rules_show/check.
- Script execution (blocked, R4d): judge() hands approved scripts back in pending {rule, event, script, timeoutSeconds, onError} (timeout filled by effectiveTimeoutSeconds ceiling 30 when the rule wrote none) and omits pending when a rule's own action already blocks. judge.ts has a local ON_ERROR_DEFAULT = 'allow'; replace it by the executor's constant when src/loops/script.ts exists. The exit-code mapping (0/2/3/1/timeout/crashed) and late verdicts are not built.

Design points interpreted rather than followed:
1. The acceptance line 'the three stop sub-entries never touch the main agent' vs design sec 3.6/13 (F86): the design says the main agent's call that dispatches a GLM subagent IS queued by glm-peak-stop-dispatch (the held party is the subagent). Followed the design: glm-peak-stop and glm-peak-stop-scripts never touch the main agent; stop-dispatch queues a GLM dispatch whoever dispatches. A spec pins both, and pins that every other main-agent call has the same verdict at all three levels and in peak, off-peak and unreadable.
2. 'no action never with block' (FEAT text) read in 0.9 terms: a rule on rules.step (the 0.8 rule with no action) only pairs with inform, and a gating event never pairs with inform. Both directions are tested.
3. A person's rule that is only a role/model filter plus queue on gate.tool-call is NOT refused: design sec 12 refuses the ticketPerSession flag and the glmSpend filter, and defines the 'any tool' class by the flag.
4. RULES_TOOL_NAMES is added now (design puts it in tool-names.ts and the stop entry needs the exemption); the contract test that pins the row's registration to it is left to the rules row step.
5. Types: GateEvent/RulesEvent live in events.ts (model.ts imports them) so model.ts and events.ts have no cycle; RuleTrigger is not exported (knip); there is no RuleDraft type; CatalogEntry has no 'lists' (M7 gate) and no 'mode' (always enforce, nothing to carry); BuiltinRule.action excludes ScriptAction and toldBy is typed HealthRow; CatalogEntry.plugin is the constant 'dsh-hourness' for every entry (all rows listed are in HOURNESS_ROWS, a spec checks that) instead of a lookup with a dead fallback.
6. Clock condition: days are ISO weekdays of the day the window BEGAN (after midnight inside a window across midnight, yesterday counts); from == to is refused (empty or whole day); tz absent or 'local' means the zone of the process (Date.getTimezoneOffset); to is exclusive, from inclusive, minute resolution.
7. validateRule script file rule: '<anything>/scripts/<rule id>.<suffix of lang>' with no .., no backslash, not absolute; the rules directory is configurable so its prefix is not checked.
8. judge(): lifetime kind 'session' (ended when the host releases the session) is not judged here (the judge has no host state); ttl, until, status and session scope (the call's session must equal sessionId) are. A rule that listens to several events counts once; for a script not run, each event has its own failure default and the blocking one wins.
9. gateEvents: args copy limit counts UTF-16 code units (65536), not bytes; 'args' is not declared in the event table (the declaration vocabulary has no object type), cwd and argsTruncated are declared as non-filterable fields.
10. Human-facing strings (validation messages, catalog titles, default rule title and reason) are Chinese as in the design; model-facing strings (the refused-script reason, signal unknown reasons) are English.

Not built, as the plan says: rules_propose-dependent validation (remove/repin/detector actions: 'measure' is refused as detector-only), the exit-code mapping of scripts, late verdicts, rules_show and checkCall text, the row, tools and commands.
